regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"India GDP at 7.8% YoY looks like acceleration — but the RBI's own forecast sits at 6.7% YoY, a 110bps gap that reflects the statistical discrepancy between GDP and GVA, not genuine output surprise. PMI composite at 54.6 is services-led (54.5) while manufacturing slips to 52.8; IIP overall at 6.7% YoY is decelerating from 8.8% last month even as capital goods surge 16.1% YoY. The quality of growth is bifurcating: investment is real, but the consumption engine is running on credit, not income.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"Headline CPI at 4.45% YoY is the wrong number to watch — core CPI at 3.9% YoY sits at the 28th percentile, meaning underlying demand pressure is benign. The problem is fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY, a 95th-percentile print, with WPI at 9.92% YoY signalling that producer margins are being squeezed before the consumer feels it. Invert the RBI's comfort: if fuel stays at Brent $106/bbl, the 2-quarter lag feeds into core CPI by Q1 FY28 — and the RBI will have cut rates into that print.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1% YoY; CD ratio 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth of 10.8% YoY is a 630bps divergence that the CD ratio at 81.4% — 75th percentile historically — only partially captures. The last time India sustained a CD ratio above 80% while the repo rate was being held was FY14; within 12 months, external shocks forced an emergency policy reversal. Today's relief valve is NBFC credit at 14.9% YoY and wholesale funding — but corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month is at a new series low, meaning the relief valve is narrowing, not widening.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. with RBI's own inflation forecast revised up to 5.1% YoY leaves the real rate at approximately 15bps — barely positive, and insufficient to anchor inflation expectations if fuel feeds through. The RBI is on pause, but the pause is increasingly asymmetric: cutting risks importing inflation via INR depreciation; holding risks choking a credit cycle that is already funding-constrained. The rate signal for housing is mildly supportive — average home loan rate at 7.25% p.a. is at the 25th percentile — but affordability at 0.42× price-to-income is at a decade low.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY with capacity utilisation rising to 77.4% of capacity — up from 75.6% — is the most credible capex signal in the dataset: manufacturers don't invest until utilisation clears 75%, and it just did. Credit to industry at 20% YoY and to services at 22.9% YoY confirms that financing is following the physical signal, not leading it. The inversion: core sector at 5.4% YoY is decelerating from 6.0%, meaning the infrastructure backbone of the capex cycle is softening even as the manufacturing tip accelerates.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹199853 cr/mo; PV 16% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹1,99,853 cr / month is a 71st-percentile print — strong, but the question is how much is genuine demand versus GST-to-GST formalization of existing informal spend. Passenger vehicle sales at 16% YoY and two-wheeler at 19.7% YoY suggest the demand is real and broad-based across urban discretionary and rural mobility. But credit card growth at 2.3% YoY — down from 5.6% — is the tell: urban consumers are pulling back on revolving credit even as they buy vehicles, suggesting the consumption surge is asset-linked, not lifestyle-driven.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 10.8% YoY creates a 350 bps divergence. CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (down from 82.5% prior month) but still elevated at 75th percentile historically. Credit-to-deposit gap has widened for 3 consecutive months: deposits lagging credit acceleration signals funding stress. NBFC credit growth at 14.9% YoY (up from 10.6% YoY) and corporate bond issuance at 18,700 ₹ cr / month (at 0% lo percentile — a new series low) indicate wholesale funding is the only relief valve.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios > 45% — they will poach deposits from smaller lenders. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities; liquidity tightening will force margin compression or credit rationing. RBI will likely cut rates in Q2 FY27 to ease deposit pressure, not growth concerns. Position for a 50 bps cut by June.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile is historically tight. The last time it was this elevated (2022–23), RBI tightened liquidity and rates rose 250 bps. This time, the direction is opposite — RBI will ease to prevent a credit crunch.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Cycle Firing on All Cylinders","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY (latest) with capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6% prior month) — both at 52nd and 74th percentiles respectively. Capacity utilisation has risen 2 consecutive months, signalling manufacturers are running hot and will invest to expand. Core sector growth at 5.4% YoY (down from 6% prior month) is moderating but remains positive. Credit to industry at 20% YoY (up from 6.5% YoY) and credit to services at 22.9% YoY (up from 10.2% YoY) show capex financing is accelerating across both manufacturing and services.","implication":"Overweight capital goods, cement, and steel stocks. Domestic equipment makers (Cummins, Kirloskar, Escorts) will see order book expansion. Infrastructure contractors (L&T, Larsen & Toubro) should see margin expansion as utilisation rates support pricing power. Avoid commodity-heavy capex plays until oil prices stabilise below $100/bbl.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is at the 74th percentile — the last time it was this high (2021–22), capex growth accelerated 18 months later. This is a leading indicator of sustained investment.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"Affluent Money Entering Via SIP Backdoor","data_text":"SIP inflows at 32,297 ₹ cr / month (up from 31,961 ₹ cr / month, rising 2 consecutive months) at 92nd percentile. SIP accounts at 100.18 mn (up from 99.06 mn) at 82nd percentile. But SIP AUM at 18.62 ₹ lakh cr (up from 18.21 ₹ lakh cr, rising 2 consecutive months) at 93rd percentile. Average SIP AUM per account = 18.62 ÷ 100.18 = ₹18.59 lakh — up 18.6% YoY. SIP YoY growth at 14% YoY (down from 16% YoY) but absolute inflows accelerating. MF AUM at 87.08 ₹ lakh cr (rising 2 consecutive months) at 86th percentile. DII equity net at 58,502 ₹ cr net / month (up from 35,099 ₹ cr net / month, rising 2 consecutive months) at 100% hi percentile.","implication":"This is late-cycle behaviour. Retail is not entering; affluent HNI money is. Average ticket size rising 18.6% YoY while account growth is only 1.1% signals wealth concentration. Reduce exposure to mass-market consumption plays (FMCG, retail). Overweight luxury goods, premium auto, and wealth management services. Expect volatility when this cohort rotates — they have lower pain tolerance than true retail.","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 92nd percentile with rising average ticket size is a rare combination. Historically, this precedes a 12–18 month market correction as HNI money locks in gains.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens Margin Compression","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (up from 20.05% YoY) at 95th percentile — the highest in the dataset. Brent crude at 106.45 $/bbl (flat, but up 4 of last 5 months from 101.1 to 105.5 $/bbl). WTI at 94.86 $/bbl (flat, but up 4 of last 5 months from 89.15 to 92.6 $/bbl). Natural gas at 3.324 $/MMBtu (flat, but up 3 of last 5 months from 3.12 to 3.22 $/MMBtu). WPI at 9.92% YoY (up from 9.78% YoY) at 67th percentile. Headline CPI at 4.45% YoY (up from 4.38% YoY) at 41st percentile, but core CPI at 3.9% YoY (at 28th percentile lo) — inflation is energy-driven, not demand-driven.","implication":"Avoid airlines, logistics, and transport stocks until oil breaks below $100/bbl. Refiners (IOC, HPCL) will see margin compression; downstream consumers (auto, cement, chemicals) will face input cost pressure. Hedge with long gold (4,184.9 $/oz, neutral polarity) and short energy-intensive discretionary. RBI will struggle to cut rates if fuel inflation persists — expect a 25 bps cut at most in Q2 FY27.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is a structural headwind. The last time it was this high (2022), RBI kept rates on hold for 6 months despite growth concerns. Expect similar policy paralysis.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"Fed Tightening Cycle Extends, BOJ Shock Looms","data_text":"Fed funds rate at 3.75% p.a. (up from 3.63% p.a., rising 2 in a row) at 68th percentile. US 10Y Treasury yield at 5.24% yield (up from 5.22%, rising 3 of last 5 months from 5.22 to 5.31 %) at 95th percentile hi. BOJ rate at 1% p.a. (up from 0.75% p.a.) at 86th percentile hi — a shock tightening that will weaken the yen and trigger carry trade unwinds. ECB deposit rate at 2.25% p.a. (up from 2% p.a.) at 59th percentile. US core PCE at 3.01% YoY (up from 2.98% YoY) at 57th percentile. US GDP SAAR at 2.2% SAAR (up from 2.5% SAAR, but rising 2 in a row from 0.7 to 2.2 %) at 50th percentile. DXY at 102.168 index (flat, but up 3 of last 5 months from 101.9 to 102.4) at 55th percentile.","implication":"Carry trades are unwinding. BOJ's 25 bps hike is a policy shock that will weaken JPY and trigger yen-funded short positions to cover. This will strengthen DXY and weaken INR. Reduce INR exposure; hedge with long USD or short INR forwards. Avoid high-beta EM equities. US rates staying elevated (5.24% on 10Y) will keep global liquidity tight. Expect FII outflows from India if DXY breaks above 103.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"US 10Y Treasury at 95th percentile hi is a structural headwind for EM. The last time it was this high (2022), FII outflows from India totalled $15 bn. BOJ's shock tightening adds tail risk.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakening Despite Strong Domestic Flows","data_text":"INR at 95.24 ₹ (down from 95.78 ₹, but up 3 of last 5 months from 95.24 to 97.09 ₹) at 89th percentile hi — a multi-year weak level. FII equity net at 29,631 ₹ cr net / month (up from 20,200 ₹ cr net / month, up 1 of last 2 months from -3,111.9 to 29,631 ₹ cr net / month) at 83rd percentile hi. DII equity net at 58,502 ₹ cr net / month (up from 35,099 ₹ cr net / month, rising 2 in a row) at 100% hi percentile. Despite strong domestic flows (DII at all-time high), INR is weakening — this signals RBI is intervening to prevent appreciation and protect export competitiveness. India VIX at 14.12 index (down from 15.25, down 3 of last 5 months from 15.28 to 14.38) at 9th percentile lo — complacency is high.","implication":"RBI is defending INR at 95.50 ₹ but will allow gradual depreciation to 96.50 ₹ to support exports. Do not chase INR strength; it is artificial. Exporters should hedge at 96.00 ₹ or weaker. Importers should cover at current levels. FII flows are strong but fragile — a 50 bps Fed cut would reverse them instantly. Reduce INR duration; prefer short-term hedges.","pct_10y":89,"pct_note":"INR at 89th percentile weak despite DII inflows at 100% hi is a red flag. RBI's intervention is masking structural weakness from oil imports and carry trade unwinds. This is unsustainable.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Surge Masks Structural Vacancy Crisis","data_text":"Office absorption at 14.1 mn sq ft / quarter (up from 11.2 mn sq ft / quarter, up 3 of last 5 quarters from 4.02 to 14.1 mn sq ft / quarter) but tagged as strong-negative signal with score -86. Office vacancy at 14.37% vacant (down from 14.74%, down 3 of last 5 quarters from 16% to 14.37%) at 41st percentile mid. Retail mall vacancy at 4.8% vacant (down from 5%, down 2 of last 5 quarters from 5.7 to 4.8%) at 7th percentile lo — retail is healing. But office absorption is concentrated in Bangalore (rent at 103.6 ₹/sqft/mo, up from 102.6 ₹/sqft/mo) and Mumbai (rent at 135.8 ₹/sqft/mo, up from 130.4 ₹/sqft/mo). Nifty IT at flat YTD despite office absorption surge. GCC (Global Capability Centres) are the buyer, not traditional IT services. IT services companies are consolidating footprints, not expanding. Unsold residential inventory at 630,600 units (up from 616,000 units, up 3 of last 4 quarters) at 65th percentile mid — residential is stalling despite home loan disbursements at 16,096 ₹ cr / quarter (up from 15,475 ₹ cr / quarter) at 0% lo percentile (new series).","implication":"Commercial real estate is decoupling from IT services. GCCs (Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Apple) are the structural buyer of office space, not IT services. This means office rents will stay elevated but IT services companies will see margin pressure from real estate cost inflation without corresponding revenue growth. Underweight IT services; overweight commercial REIT exposure (Embassy, Mindspace) but only for GCC-heavy portfolios. Residential real estate is in a structural downturn — affordability at 0.42 × price ÷ income (up from 0.4, up 3 of last 5 quarters from 2.8 to 4.1) signals pricing has decoupled from income growth. Avoid residential developers; focus on commercial and logistics REITs.","pct_10y":0,"pct_note":"This is a structural shift. GCCs are replacing IT services as the primary driver of office demand. IT services companies are rightsizing, not expanding. This will pressure margins for 18–24 months as lease renewals hit higher rents. Residential affordability at 0% lo percentile is a generational low — expect a 15–20% price correction in tier-2 cities over 2 years.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP, 3.9% Core — Two Economies, One Headline

The facts:

  • India GDP at 7.8% YoY accelerates from 7.4% YoY, but RBI's own forecast is 6.7% YoY — a 110bps gap that is statistical, not structural.
  • PMI Composite at 54.6 (83rd percentile) is services-driven; manufacturing PMI slipped to 52.8 while IIP overall decelerated to 6.7% YoY from 8.8% YoY.
  • Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (74th percentile, up from 75.6%) crossed the private-investment threshold — the capex signal is genuine.
  • But core CPI at 3.9% YoY (28th percentile) and credit card growth at 2.3% YoY (down from 5.6% YoY) signal that the consumer underneath the headline is more cautious than the PMI suggests.

The tension: The GDP headline and the RBI forecast disagree by 110bps; the PMI and IIP disagree on direction. Growth is real in investment, uncertain in consumption, and overstated in the headline.

Bottom line: Watch IIP capital goods for a second consecutive 15%+ YoY print — confirmation that the utilisation-to-investment transmission is holding, not a one-month spike.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US 10Y at 5.24% — Bond Market Tightening Where the Fed Has Not

The facts:

  • US 10Y Treasury at 5.24% yield (95th percentile), rising three of the last five sessions — bond market is doing the Fed's work without a meeting.
  • Fed Funds at 3.75% p.a. (68th percentile) with US Core PCE at 3.01% YoY (57th percentile) — the Fed is behind the curve on the long end.
  • BOJ rate jumped to 1.0% p.a. from 0.75% p.a. (86th percentile) — a shock tightening that begins unwinding the yen carry trade that has funded EM equity inflows for two years.
  • But US PMI Composite at 56 (84th percentile) and Euro Stoxx 50 at 6,167 (100th percentile) signal DM equities are still pricing re-acceleration that the bond market is actively contradicting.

The tension: DM equities at or near all-time percentiles; DM bond yields also at multi-decade highs. One of them is wrong — and the BOJ's move just shortened the timeline for resolution.

Bottom line: If US 10Y sustains above 5.30% yield, EM carry unwinds accelerate — watch FII equity net flows for the first reversal signal.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

Deposit Gap Widens as the Only Relief Valve Dries Up

The facts:

  • Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY vs deposit growth at 10.8% YoY — a 630bps divergence with CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (75th percentile historically).
  • Corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month is at a new series low (0th percentile) — the wholesale funding alternative is contracting, not expanding.
  • NBFC credit growth at 14.9% YoY (up from 10.6% YoY) is accelerating into a tightening funding environment — the risk is being pushed downstream, not resolved.
  • But SIP inflows at ₹32,297 cr / month (92nd percentile) and MF AUM at ₹87.08 lakh cr (86th percentile) show household savings are flowing into equity, not bank deposits.

The tension: Households are saving into mutual funds rather than bank deposits, structurally widening the CD gap even as credit demand accelerates. The system is funding long-term loans with short-term equity inflows.

Bottom line: Watch for RBI macro-prudential action — a risk-weight increase on NBFC lending or unsecured credit would be the first circuit-breaker; the CD ratio at 83%+ is the trigger level.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

NRI Premium Demand Holds; REITs Disconnected from Absorption Reality

The facts:

  • NRI buying is RISING — NRI share of residential purchases at 20% (up from 15%, +5 pp), with NRI share within premium/luxury at 25%; remittances at $140 bn (12.8% YoY) are the funding source.
  • Hyderabad leads city momentum: sales +15% YoY with launches +120% YoY — a supply surge into strong demand that will test pricing within 6–8 quarters.
  • Office absorption at 14.1 mn sq ft / quarter is GCC-driven (41% of occupier mix) — IT services at 15% of mix is consolidating, not expanding; Nifty IT flat YTD confirms the divergence.
  • But Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit, Mindspace at ₹345/unit, and Brookfield at ₹263/unit are all down sharply from prior prints — REIT investors are not pricing the absorption surge.

The tension: Office absorption is at a multi-quarter high driven by GCCs, but REIT unit prices are falling — the market is correctly distinguishing between GCC lease demand (long-term, credit-worthy) and IT services vacancy risk (rising).

Bottom line: Overweight residential developers with Hyderabad and Bengaluru exposure; avoid office REITs until IT services headcount stabilises and vacancy below 12% vacant nationally.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three Fuses, One Detonator — BOJ Is the Match

The facts:

  • BOJ rate shock to 1.0% p.a. (86th percentile) triggers yen carry unwind — every 5% yen appreciation historically pulls $20–30bn from EM equity allocations within 60 days.
  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) with Brent at $106/bbl — if crude holds, RBI's inflation forecast of 5.1% YoY is already stale and a rate cut is off the table through FY27.
  • CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits with corporate bond issuance at a series low — if deposit growth does not accelerate to 13%+ YoY within two quarters, NBFC funding costs spike and credit growth stalls.
  • India VIX at 14.12 (9th percentile) — complacency is near a decade high precisely as three external risks are simultaneously elevated.

The tension: Domestic complacency (VIX at 9th percentile) is inversely correlated with external stress (BOJ shock, US 10Y at 95th percentile, Brent at 74th percentile) — the gap between perceived and actual risk is the widest it has been this cycle.

Bottom line: Watch FII equity net flows this week: a reversal below ₹10,000 cr net / month would confirm the BOJ carry unwind is reaching India, and VIX at 18+ would be the confirmation.

"}
